newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: PRESS DIGEST - Pakistan newspapers - December 30.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Pakistan newspapers - December 30.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the Pakistani press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- The electoral process in Pakistan received its first setback when the Islamist Jamaat-i-Islami announced its decision to boycott the February 3 elections mainly because of the failure of the caretaker government to keep corrupt elements out of the electoral process.
- Caretaker Prime Minister Meraj Khalid speaking at a function endorsed the political objectives of Imran Khan and asked people to support his political campaign.
- Olympian Qazi Mohibur Rehman, former captain of the national hockey team, died of cancer at a local hospital.
- The Economic Committee of the cabinet decided to urgently import additional 600,000 tonnes of wheat to stabilise prices. The Committee deferred the plan of increasing gas prices by 25 percent.
- Former chief minister of the southern Sindh province Abdullah Shah was released on bail.
- The federal government will sell its remaining stake in the privatised Muslim Commercial Bank and Allied Bank of Pakistan in January, sources said.
- The Economic Coordination Committee of the Cabinet approved a proposal to carry out detailed feasibility study of a 500 megawatt to 700 megawatt hydel power plant in Azad Kashmir.
- The government on Sunday released a list of 12,839 loan defaulters and 1,413 people whose loans were written off in the past.
- The Economic Coordination Committee of the cabinet has asked the state-run Utility Stores Corporation to import 25,000 tonnes of sugar to meet the shortages.
